highlights: Coverage: 317 of 548 inventory items were checked this run, 311 against outside sources (198 no change, 31 changed, 72 unresolved, mostly comparative wording or a primary source not found, 10 inaccessible) and 6 internally. All 139 items never verified before were attempted; 71 now pass and 68 remain open with what is missing recorded. 218 sources behind earlier checks were re-fetched (194 by plain download, 24 in headless Chromium; 200 retrieved): 34 had genuinely changed, and the 180 items resting on them were re-verified. No audit ran on 13, 19, 26 Oct or 2 Nov; this run covers the whole period since the 10 Oct baseline.

40 new proposals (P-0149 to P-0188). 39 await your decision: 24 corrections, 1 new entry (Japan AI Basic Plan, P-0178) and 14 questions, each with drafted options and a recommendation; P-0187 is held until its source can be opened. The largest: Meta's framework is now v2.1, the 'Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework' (P-0149); SpaceX acquired xAI, whose site now says SpaceXSI (P-0151, recommended: keep the name and add a note); Colorado SB 24-205 was not repealed before 30 Jun 2026 and a court order bars enforcement (P-0181); Illinois' Agency can levy its own penalties (P-0180); the EU AI Office has no pre-deployment access power (P-0162).

Discovery: proposed new entries for Japan's AI Basic Plan (P-0178) and the AEF-1 evaluator standard now cited by the EU AI Office (P-0172, a question). The White House Accord on Super Intelligence (29 Sep 2026, six labs) is drafted as an addition (P-0187) but held as 'needs source access': only an archive copy was found, not an official one. Leads awaiting access: California SB 813 / AB 1405 (independent verification organizations), New York RAISE implementation, Korea's July 2026 amendment, Singapore's Online Safety Commission.

Not retrievable this week: California's legislature site, the Council of Europe, openai.com, ico.org.uk, Ofcom, FTC and eSafety refused automated clients even in headless Chromium; items resting on them were marked inaccessible, or kept on their 10 Oct passages where noted. Two answers saved on the page on 13 Oct (P-0134 accept, P-0137 option b) belong to the lost 12 Oct run and are not in the ledger, so they were not acted on; new numbering starts at P-0149 so those IDs are never reused.

Nothing was applied: there were no new answers to current proposals, so the map's content date stays 11 Oct 2026. Tooling note: source fetch does not request decompressed content, so gzip-only pages (deepmind.google) cache unreadable bytes; saved copies were used instead.
